_comment: ADOPTER EXAMPLE (rc.39 · flow-plan Phase 5.2) — the exposure register for the bundled CHG-2026-0042, mounted as docs/governance/feature-flags.json. It exists so scripts/feature-flag-check.mjs verifies something REAL: the change-example compiles HIGH, the regulated-bank profile declares the exposure_control capability at high tier, and mandatory-when-compiled therefore makes this register non-optional in the adopted layout. Without a worked example the gate would only ever have been exercised against tmp fixtures, which is the vacuum every *-example/ directory in this bundle exists to fill. Note what the flag_key is: the SAME lever governance/service-readiness.template.json names as `kill_switch.mechanism`, which is what makes the R3 kill-switch drill evidence for this control too — one switch, drilled once, cited twice.

flags.kill_path: flag console → credit.decisioning.enabled → off; in-flight applications drain to the manual underwriting queue (runbooks/credit-origination-rollback.md §kill-switch)
flags._expires_comment: ADOPT: a real flag's life is short — one or two releases. The date here is far out ON PURPOSE, for the reason the pattern expiry states in profiles/regulated-bank.json: a shipped fixture with a 90-day life is a build that turns red on a calendar, and a check that turns red on a calendar gets deleted rather than renewed. The bundle's CI restamps this field per run to prove BOTH directions (warned, then expired-and-blocked) without the date being load-bearing.
flags.notes: The affordability model is in the decision path behind this flag. OFF means every application routes to manual underwriting — the pre-change behaviour — so 'off' is a working product, not a broken one. That is the property that makes the kill path real.
